translations.text: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in the prophets: “Look, I am sending my messenger before you, who will prepare your way.”
“The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”
John appeared in the wilderness, baptizing and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
The whole region of Judea and the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and they were all baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
John was clothed in camel hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and ate locusts and wild honey.
He proclaimed, “Someone more powerful than I is coming after me. I am not worthy to bend down and untie the straps of his sandals.
I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
Immediately, as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit descending upon him like a dove.
A voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; I am well pleased with you.”
Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
He was there in the wilderness for twenty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and angels served him.
After John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom of God
and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent and believe in the gospel.”
As he walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, Simon’s brother, casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
Going on from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee and his brother John, who were also in a boat, mending their nets.
Immediately he called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and followed him.
They entered Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath he taught them in the synagogue.
They were amazed at his teaching, for he taught as someone with authority, and not like their scribes.
There was a man in the synagogue with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
“Leave us alone! What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent and come out of him!”
And the unclean spirit convulsed him and came out of him with a loud cry.
And they were all amazed and debated among themselves, saying, “What is this? What is this new teaching? He commands even the unclean spirits with authority, and they obey him.”
And news of him immediately spread throughout the whole region of Galilee.
And immediately after leaving the synagogue, they entered the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Now Simon’s mother-in-law lay burning with a fever, and they immediately told him about her.
And he went to her, took her by the hand, and raised her up. Immediately the fever left her, and she served them.
When evening came and the sun was setting, they brought to him all who were sick and possessed by demons.
And the whole town had gathered at the door.
And he healed many who were sick with various diseases and drove out many demons. He would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
And very early in the morning, at daybreak, Jesus rose, went out, and departed to a deserted place. There he prayed.
And Simon and those who were with him went after him.
And when they found him, they said to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
And he said to them, “Let us go to the nearby villages and towns, so that I may preach there too, for that is why I came out.”
And he preached in their synagogues throughout Galilee and drove out demons.
And a man with leprosy came to him, pleading with him and falling to his knees, saying to him, “If you are willing, you can make me clean.”
And Jesus, moved with compassion, stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him, “I am willing. Be clean.”
And when he had spoken, the leprosy immediately left the man, and he became clean.
And after sternly warning him, he immediately sent him away.
And he said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone. Instead, go and show yourself to the high priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
But he went out and began to proclaim it widely and spread the news, so that he could no longer enter a town openly, but stayed outside in deserted places. And people came to him from everywhere.
And after some days Jesus entered Capernaum again, and word spread that he was in the house.
And immediately many gathered, so that there was no longer room, not even in front of the door. And he spoke the word to them.
And they came to him bringing a paralyzed man, carried by four people.
And because they could not get near him on account of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where he was. After digging through it, they lowered the bed on which the paralyzed man lay.
And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
Some of the scribes were sitting there, thinking in their hearts,
“Why does this man speak blasphemies like this? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Jesus immediately knew in his spirit that they were thinking this within themselves, and he said to them, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your bed, and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins on earth”—and he said to the paralyzed man,
“I tell you, get up, pick up your bed, and go home.”
He immediately got up, picked up his bed, and went out in front of everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
He went out again to the sea. The whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
As Jesus passed by, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.
As he reclined at the meal in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many of them, and they were following him.
The scribes and Pharisees, seeing him eating with tax collectors and sinners, said to his disciples, “Why does he eat and drink with sinners?”
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “Healthy people do not need a doctor, but sick people do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. They came and said to him, “Why do John’s disciples and the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?”
Jesus said to them, “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days.
No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. Otherwise, the new patch pulls away from the old garment, and the tear becomes worse.
No one pours new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the new wine will burst them, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, new wine must be poured into new wineskins.”
Jesus was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to make their way along, plucking heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, “Look, why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and was hungry, both he and those who were with him?
How he entered the house of God when Abiathar was high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which only priests were permitted to eat, and also gave some to those who were with him?”
He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for humankind, not humankind for the Sabbath. Therefore the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
He entered the synagogue again, and a man with a withered hand was there.
They watched him to see whether he would heal the man on the Sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
He said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand here in the middle.”
And he said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?” But they remained silent. And
looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored, as healthy as the other.
And immediately the Pharisees went out and took counsel with the Herodians against him, planning how they might destroy him.
But Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea. And a large crowd from Galilee followed him, and from Judea,
and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond the Jordan. And a great multitude from around Tyre and Sidon, hearing how much he was doing, came to him.
And he told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush him.
For he had healed many, so that all who had afflictions pressed upon him, wanting to touch him.
And whenever the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, saying, “You are the Christ, the Son of God!”
And he sternly warned them not to make him known.
And he went up the mountain and called those whom he himself wanted, and they came to him.
And he appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out by him to preach,
and to have authority to heal illnesses and cast out demons.
And he gave Simon the name Peter;
and James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, to whom he gave the name Boanerges, which means “Sons of Thunder”;
and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. And they went into a house.
And the crowds gathered again, so that they could not even eat bread.
And when his own people heard about it, they went out to seize him, for they were saying, “He is out of his mind.”
And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the ruler of the demons he casts out demons.”
And he called them to him and spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan?
And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a household is divided against itself, that household cannot stand.
And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but has come to an end.
No one can enter a strong man’s house and plunder his possessions unless he first binds the strong man. Then he will plunder his house.
Truly I tell you, all sins will be forgiven the children of men, and whatever blasphemies they utter.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never have forgiveness, but is liable to eternal judgment.
For they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”
Then his mother and brothers came, and standing outside, they sent someone to him to call him.
A crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him, “Look, your mother and your brothers and sisters are outside looking for you.”
He answered them, saying, “Who is my mother, or who are my brothers?”
Looking around at those standing around him, he said, “Here are my mother and my brothers.
For whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.”
Again he began to teach beside the sea. A large crowd gathered around him, so that he got into a boat and sat in it on the sea, while the whole crowd was on the land beside the sea.
He taught them many things in parables, and in his teaching he said to them:
“Listen! A sower went out to sow.
As he sowed, some seeds fell on the path, and birds came and ate them up.
Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil, and immediately it sprouted because the soil was not deep.
But when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.
Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it produced no crop.
Other seed fell on good soil and produced a crop, sprouting and growing and yielding thirtyfold, fortyfold, and a hundredfold.”
And he said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.”
When he was alone, those who were with him, together with the Twelve, asked him about the parable.
He said to them, “You have been given knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to those outside, everything comes in parables,
so that they may look and look but not see, and hear and hear but not understand, lest they turn back and their sins be forgiven them.”
He said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?
The sower sows the word.
These are the ones along the path where the word is sown: when they hear, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word sown in their hearts.
Likewise, these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy.
But they have no root in themselves and last only a short time. Then, when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately fall away.
And these are the ones sown among thorns: those who hear the word.
And the worries of this age, the deceitfulness of wealth, and desires for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And these are the ones sown on good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.
And he said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under a basket or under a bed? Is it not to be put on a lampstand?”
For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor has anything been kept secret except to come to light.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
And he said to them, “Pay attention to what you hear. The measure you use will be used for you, and more will be added to you who hear.”
For whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.
And he said, “The kingdom of God is like this: a man scatters seed on the ground.”
And he sleeps and rises, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how.
For the earth produces a crop by itself: first the stalk, then the ear, then the wheat in the ear.
But when the crop is ripe, he immediately sends in the sickle, because the harvest has come.
And he said, “What shall we compare the kingdom of God to, or what parable shall we use to describe it?”
It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown in the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on earth.
And when it is sown, it grows and becomes larger than all the garden plants and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can nest in its shade.
And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
He did not speak to them without a parable, but privately he explained everything to his disciples.
And on that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let us cross to the other side.”
And leaving the crowd, they took him with them just as he was, in the boat. Other boats were also with him.
And a great windstorm arose, and the waves poured into the boat, so that it was already about to sink.
And he himself was in the stern, asleep on a cushion. And they woke him and said to him, “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”
And he rose and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, “Be silent! Be still!” And the wind died down, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
And they were filled with great fear and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?”
And they came to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gadarenes.
And when he came out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit immediately met him from among the tombs.
He lived among the tombs, and no one could bind him, even with an iron chain.
For he had often been bound with shackles and iron chains, but he tore the chains apart and broke the shackles to pieces. No one could subdue him.
And constantly, day and night, he was among the tombs and in the mountains, crying out and striking himself with stones.
But when he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before him.
And he cried out in a loud voice, saying, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore you by God, do not torment me!”
For he was saying to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
And he asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”
And he begged him earnestly not to send them out of the region.
Now a large herd of pigs was grazing there near the mountain.
And all the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter them.”

And Jesus immediately gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea. There were about two thousand of them, and they drowned in the sea.
And those tending the pigs fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside. And people came to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been possessed by demons, the one who had had the Legion, sitting there clothed and in his right mind. And they were afraid.
And those who had seen it told them what had happened to the man possessed by demons, and about the pigs.
And they began to beg him to leave their territory.
And as he was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by demons begged him to let him stay with him.
But Jesus did not allow him. Instead, he said to him, “Go home to your own people and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you.”
And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed.
And when Jesus had crossed again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him. And he was beside the sea.
And behold, one of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came. When he saw him, he fell at his feet.
And he begged him earnestly, saying, “My daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be healed and live.”
And he went with him. A large crowd followed him and pressed in on him.
And there was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She had suffered much under many physicians and had spent everything she had, but had gained no benefit. Instead, she had grown worse.
Having heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his garment.
For she said, “If I touch even his clothes, I will be healed.”
And immediately the source of her bleeding dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
And immediately Jesus, sensing within himself that power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched my clothes?”
And his disciples said to him, “You see the crowd pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
And he looked around to see the woman who had done this.
But the woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
And Jesus said to her, “Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace, and be free of your affliction.”
And while he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue leader’s house, saying, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher?”
But Jesus, immediately hearing what was being said, said to the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid; only believe.”
And he allowed no one to follow him except Peter, James, and John, the brother of James.
And he came to the synagogue leader’s house and saw a commotion, with people weeping and wailing loudly.
And he went in and said to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The girl is not dead but asleep.”
And they laughed at him. But he put them all outside, took the girl’s father and mother and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.
And he took the girl by the hand and said to her, “Talitha koum,” which means, “Girl, I say to you, get up.”
And immediately the girl got up and walked, for she was twelve years old. And they were utterly astonished.
And he strictly ordered them not to let anyone know about this, and told them to give her something to eat.
And he left that place and came to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.

And when the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue. And many who heard him were astonished, saying, “Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom given to him? And how are such miracles performed by his hands?”
“Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
And Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own house.”
He could not perform any miracle there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
And he marveled at their unbelief. And he went around the villages, teaching.
And he called the Twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over unclean spirits.
And he instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff—no bag, no bread, and no copper money in their belts.
But they were to wear sandals and not put on two tunics.
And he said to them, “Whenever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.”

“And whoever will not welcome you or listen to you, when you leave that place, shake off the dust under your feet as a testimony against them. Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom or Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.”
And they went out and preached that people should repent.
And they drove out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
And King Herod heard the news about Jesus, for his name had become known. And he said, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and that is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
Others said that he was Elijah, that he was like one of the prophets.
But when Herod heard this, he said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
For Herod himself had sent men to arrest John and had bound him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, whom he had married.
For John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have the wife of your brother Philip.”
And Herodias was angry with him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and protected him. And when he listened to him, he did many things, and he listened to him gladly.
And a suitable day came, when Herod held a birthday banquet for his nobles, military commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.
And when Herodias’s daughter came in and danced, pleasing Herod and those dining with him, the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask for, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”
She went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” And she said, “The head of John the Baptist.”
And she immediately hurried in to the king and made her request, saying, “I want you to give me [?] the head of John the Baptist on a platter.”
And the king was deeply grieved, but because of his oaths and those dining with him, he did not want to refuse her.
And the king immediately sent a mounted soldier and ordered him to bring John’s head.
He went and beheaded him in prison, and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl. And the girl gave it to her mother.
And when his disciples heard about it, they took his body and laid it in a tomb.
And the apostles gathered around Jesus and told him everything they had done and everything they had taught.
And he said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
And they went away by boat to a deserted place by themselves.
And people saw them leaving, and many recognized them. They ran there on foot from all the towns and arrived ahead of them.
And when Jesus came out, he saw a large crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.
When much time had already passed, his disciples came to him and said, “This is a deserted place, and the hour is already late.
Send them away so that they can go into the surrounding farms and villages and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.”
But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to him, “Are we to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”
He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” When they had found out, they said, “Five loaves and two fish.”
He ordered them to have all the people sit down in groups on the green grass.
They sat down in groups of a hundred and of fifty.

Taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven and blessed them. He broke the loaves and gave them to his disciples to set before the people. He also divided the two fish among them all.
They all ate and were satisfied.
They gathered twelve baskets full of broken pieces, and also some of the fish.
There were five thousand men who had eaten the bread.
Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while he himself sent the crowds away.
After saying goodbye to them, he went up the mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on land.
He saw them struggling to row, for the wind was against them. Around the fourth watch of the night, he came toward them, walking on the sea, and intended to pass them by.
When they saw him walking on the sea, they thought he was a ghost and cried out.
For they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke to them and said, “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
He got into the boat with them, and the wind died down. They were utterly astonished within themselves and filled with amazement.
For they had not understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.
After crossing over, they came to the land of Gennesaret and moored the boat.
When they got out of the boat, the people immediately recognized him.
They ran throughout that whole region and began bringing the sick on their beds to wherever they heard he was.
Wherever he went, into villages, towns, or farms, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him to let them touch even the fringe of his garment. All who touched him were healed.
The Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him.
When they saw some of his disciples eating bread with unclean hands—that is, unwashed hands—they found fault.
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands, rubbing them, holding to the tradition of the elders.
And when they come from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash. There are also many other things they have received and observe: the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches.
Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, “Why do your disciples not follow the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands?”
He answered them, “Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘These people honor me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
They worship me in vain, teaching human commandments as doctrines.’
For you have abandoned the commandment of God and hold to human traditions: the washing of pitchers and cups. And you do many other such things.”
And he said to them, “You are very good at rejecting the commandment of God so that you may keep your own tradition!
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever curses father or mother must be put to death.’
But you say that if someone says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever benefit you might have received from me is Corban,’ meaning a gift,
then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,
nullifying the word of God through your tradition that you have handed down. And you do many other such things.”
And he called the whole crowd to him and said to them, “Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that can defile him by entering him. Rather, the things that come out of him are what defile a person.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
And when he had left the crowd and entered the house, his disciples asked him about the parable.
And he said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not understand that whatever enters a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and passes out into the latrine, cleansing all food?”
And he said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles him.
For from within, from the human heart, come thoughts, adulteries, sexual immorality, murders,
thefts, acts of injustice, wickedness, deceit, indecency, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.
All these evil things come from within and defile a person.”
And he left that place and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon. He entered a house and did not want anyone to know, but he could not remain hidden.
For a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him, came, and fell at his feet.
The woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician by birth. And she begged him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
But Jesus said to her, “Let the children be fed first, for it is not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
She answered him, “Yes, Lord, for even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
And he said to her, “Because of this answer, go. The demon has left your daughter.”
And she went home and found the girl lying on the bed, and the demon gone.
And Jesus again left the regions of Tyre and Sidon and came to the Sea of Galilee, through the region of the Decapolis.
And they brought him a deaf man who had difficulty speaking, and begged him to lay his hand on him.
And he took him aside, away from the crowd, put his fingers into his ears, and spat and touched his tongue.
And looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him, “Ephphatha,” which means, “Be opened.”
And immediately his ears were opened, the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he spoke clearly.
And he ordered them to tell no one. But the more he ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.
And they were utterly amazed, saying, “He does everything well. He makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.”
In those days, when there was again a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples and said to them,
“I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already stayed with me for three days and have nothing to eat.
And if I send them home without food, they will grow faint on the way, for some of them have come from far away.”
And his disciples answered him, “Where can anyone get enough bread to feed these people here in the wilderness?”
And he asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
And he told the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then he took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to serve. And they set them before the crowd.
They also had a few small fish. And after blessing them, he said, “Serve these too.”
And they ate and were satisfied, and they gathered seven baskets of leftover pieces.
There were about four thousand who had eaten. And he sent them away.
And immediately he got into the boat with his disciples and came to the region of Dalmanutha.
And the Pharisees came out and began to argue with him, seeking a sign from heaven from him to test him.
And he sighed deeply in his spirit and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
And he left them, got into the boat again, and went to the other side.
And they forgot to take bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
And he warned them, saying, “Watch out! Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
And they discussed it with one another, saying, “It is because we have no bread.”
Jesus, knowing this, said to them, “Why are you thinking about having no bread? Do you still not perceive or understand? Are your hearts hardened?”
“Do you have eyes but fail to see, and ears but fail to hear? And do you not remember?”
“When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets of broken pieces did you collect?” They said to him, “Twelve.”
“And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” They said, “Seven.”
And he said to them, “How is it that you do not understand?”
And he came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him.
Taking the blind man by the hand, he led him out of the village. He spat on his eyes, laid his hands on him, and asked him whether he could see anything.
He looked up and said, “I see people; they look like trees walking around.”
Then he again laid his hands on his eyes and made him see. His sight was restored, and he saw everything clearly.
And he sent him home, saying, “Do not go into the village or tell anyone in the village.”
Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do people say I am?”
They answered, “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and others one of the prophets.”
And he said to them, “But who do you say I am?” Peter answered him, “You are the Christ.”
And he sternly ordered them not to tell anyone about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer greatly, be put to the test by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise again on the third day.
He spoke about this openly. And Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
But he turned, looked at his disciples, and rebuked Peter, saying, “Get behind me, Satan! For you are not thinking about the things of God, but the things of human beings.”
And he called the crowd to him along with his disciples and said to them, “Whoever wants to follow me must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.”
“For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the gospel will save it.”
“For what does it benefit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his soul?”
“For what can a person give in exchange for his soul?”
“For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.”
“Truly I tell you, some of those standing here will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power.”
After six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John and led them up a high mountain by themselves. And he was transfigured before them.
And his clothes became dazzling, exceedingly white like snow, whiter than any cloth cleaner on earth could make them.
And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with him.
Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
For he did not know what to say, because they were terrified.
And a cloud came and overshadowed them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
And suddenly, when they looked around, they saw no one with them except Jesus alone.
As they were coming down the mountain, he commanded them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
And they kept this saying to themselves, discussing what rising from the dead meant.
And they asked him, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
He answered them, “Elijah does indeed come first and restore everything. And how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer greatly and be treated with contempt?
But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wished, just as it is written about him.”
And when he came to the disciples, he saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
And immediately, when the whole crowd saw him, they were astonished and ran up to greet him.
And he asked the scribes, “What are you arguing about among yourselves?”
One of the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought you my son, who has a spirit that makes him unable to speak.
Whenever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I told your disciples to drive it out, but they could not.”
He answered him, “O faithless generation, how long will I be among you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to me.”
And they brought him to Jesus. When the spirit saw him, it immediately threw the boy into convulsions, and he fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
And Jesus asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” He said, “Since childhood.
And it has often thrown him into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, everything is possible for the one who believes.”
And immediately the child’s father cried out with tears, “I believe, Lord! Help my unbelief!”
When Jesus saw that a crowd was running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you to come out of him and never enter him again.”
And the spirit cried out, convulsed him violently, and came out. The boy became like a dead person, so that many said, “He is dead.”
But Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him up, and he stood up.
And when he had entered the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why could we not drive it out?”
And he said to them, “This kind can come out by nothing except prayer and fasting.”
And they left that place and traveled through Galilee. He did not want anyone to know.
For he was teaching his disciples and telling them, “The Son of Man will be handed over into human hands, and they will kill him. After he has been killed, he will rise on the third day.”
But they did not understand what he said and were afraid to ask him.
And he came to Capernaum. When he was in the house, he asked them, “What were you discussing among yourselves on the way?”
But they were silent, for on the way they had argued with one another about who was the greatest.
And he sat down, called the Twelve, and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.”
And he took a child and placed the child in their midst. Taking the child in his arms, he said to them,
“Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes not me but the one who sent me.”
John answered him, saying, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name who does not follow us, and we forbade him because he did not follow us.”
But Jesus said, “Do not forbid him, for no one who performs a miracle in my name can soon afterward speak evil of me.
For whoever is not against you is for you.
For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in my name because you belong to Christ—truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward.
And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a millstone put around his neck and be thrown into the sea.
And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have both hands and go into Gehenna, into the fire that cannot be put out,
where their worm does not die and the fire does not go out.
And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into Gehenna, into the fire that cannot be put out,
where their worm does not die and the fire does not go out.
And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have both eyes and go into fiery Gehenna,
where their worm does not die and the fire does not go out.
For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
Salt is good. But if salt becomes unsalty, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
And he left that place and came to the region of Judea on the other side of the Jordan. Crowds gathered around him again, and, as was his custom, he taught them again.
And the Pharisees came up and asked him whether it was lawful for a man to divorce his wife, testing him.
He answered them, “What did Moses command you?”
Moses commanded that a certificate of divorce be written and that she be sent away.
Jesus answered them, “Because of your hardness of heart, he wrote this commandment for you.
But from the beginning of creation, God made them male and female.
For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife.
And you two will become one flesh. So you are no longer two, but one flesh.
Therefore, what God has joined together, let no one separate.”
In the house, his disciples asked him again about this.
He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”
People were bringing children to him so that he might touch them, but the disciples rebuked those bringing them.
When Jesus saw this, he was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it.”
He took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.
As he was setting out on the road, a man came, knelt before him, and asked him, “Good teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Do not defraud. Honor your father and mother.”
He answered him, “Teacher, I have kept all these from my youth.”

Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “There is one thing you have not yet done. If you want to be perfect, go, sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, take up the cross, and follow me.”
But he was dismayed at these words and went away sorrowful, for he had many possessions.
Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”
The disciples were astonished at his words. But Jesus spoke again and said to them, “Children, how hard it is for those who trust in wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
They were utterly amazed and said to one another, “Who can be saved?”
Jesus looked at them and said, “For human beings it is impossible, but not for God, for all things are possible for God.”
Peter began to say to him, “Look, we have left everything and followed you.”
Jesus answered, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who leaves a house, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children, or fields for my sake and for the gospel,
who will not receive a hundredfold now, in this time—houses, brothers, sisters, a father, mothers, children, and fields, after persecution—and in the age to come, eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

They were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them. They were amazed, and those following were afraid. Jesus took the twelve aside again and began to tell them what was going to happen to him:
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles.
They will mock him and kill him, and on the third day he will rise again.”
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came forward before him and said to him, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask.”
Jesus said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said to him, “Grant that we may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory.”
Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”
They said to him, “We can.” Jesus said to them, “You will indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.
But to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to grant, but is for those for whom it has been prepared.”
When the ten heard this, they began to be indignant with James and John.
Jesus called them to him and said to them, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great men exercise authority over them.
But it must not be so among you.
Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first among you must be everyone's slave.
For the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
They came to Jericho. As he was leaving Jericho with his disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting blind beside the road, begging.
When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out and say, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Many rebuked him, telling him to be silent, but he cried out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and said to call him. They called the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage! Get up; he is calling you.”
He threw aside his clothes, got up, and came to Jesus.
Jesus answered him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabbouni, let me regain my sight.”
Jesus said to him, “Go; your faith has saved you.” Immediately he regained his sight and followed Jesus along the road.
When he drew near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples.
And he said to them, “Go into the village opposite you. As soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied up, which no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it.
And if anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs it,’ and he will immediately send it here.”
They went and found a colt tied at a door, outside at a crossroads, and they untied it.
And some of those standing there said to them, “What are you doing, untying the colt?”
They answered them as Jesus had instructed, and they let them go.
And they brought the colt to Jesus and put their cloaks on it, and he sat on it.
Many spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
And those going ahead and those following behind cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David, which comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
And Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. After looking around at everything, since it was already late, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
The next morning, as they were leaving Bethany, he became hungry.
And seeing a fig tree in leaf in the distance, he went to see whether he might find anything on it. But when he reached it, he found nothing on it except leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
And Jesus said to it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” And his disciples heard him.
And they came to Jerusalem. Jesus entered the temple and began driving out those selling and buying in the temple. He overturned the traders’ tables and the seats of those selling doves.
And he would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
And he taught them, saying, “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”
And the scribes and chief priests heard this and sought a way to destroy him, for they feared him, because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.
And when evening came, he would go out of the city.
And as they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
And Peter remembered and said to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has withered.”
And Jesus answered him, “Have faith in God.
Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Move and throw yourself into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, will have whatever he says.
Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you receive it, and it will be yours.
And whenever you stand praying, forgive if you have anything against anyone, so that your heavenly Father may also forgive you your sins.
But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your sins.”
They came again to Jerusalem. As he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, scribes, and elders came to him.
They said to him, “By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority to do these things?”
Jesus answered them, “I too will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
Where did John’s baptism come from? Was it from heaven or from human beings? Answer me.”
They discussed it among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From human beings’”—they were afraid of the people, for everyone regarded John as a prophet.
They answered Jesus, “We do not know.” “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
He began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress, and built a tower. He leased it to tenant farmers and went away.
At the proper time he sent a servant to the tenant farmers to receive from them some of the vineyard’s fruit.
But they seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
Again he sent another servant to them. They threw stones at him, wounded him in the head, and sent him away dishonored.
Again he sent another, and they killed him. And many others: some they beat, and some they killed.
He still had one son, his beloved. He sent him to them last, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
But those tenant farmers said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
They seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not read this scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
They sought to arrest him but feared the crowd, for they understood that he had spoken the parable against them. So they left him and went away.
They sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to him to trap him in what he said.

They came and said to him, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and do not concern yourself with anyone’s standing, for you do not judge people by appearances, but teach the way of God truthfully. Is it lawful to pay the tax to Caesar or not? Should we pay it or not?”
But he knew their hypocrisy and said to them, “Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius so that I may see it.”
They brought one, and he said to them, “Whose image and inscription is this?” They said to him, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus answered them, “Give back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.” And they marveled at him.
Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and questioned him, saying:
Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, his brother must marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers. The first married a wife, and when he died, he left no offspring.
The second married her and died, and he too left no offspring. The third did the same.
All seven married her and left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died.
So in the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as their wife.
Jesus answered them, “Is this not why you are mistaken: because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
As for the dead being raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living. So you are greatly mistaken.”
One of the scribes came up and heard them debating. Seeing that Jesus had answered them well, he asked him, “Which commandment is first of all?”
Jesus said to him, “The first of all the commandments is: ‘Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first of all the commandments.
The second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
The scribe said to him, “Well said, Teacher. You have spoken truly that he is one, and there is no other besides him.

And to love him with all the heart, with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is greater than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
When Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question him any further.
Then Jesus said as he taught in the temple, “How do the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
For David himself said through the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”’
David himself calls him Lord, so how is he his son?” And the great crowds listened to him with delight.
In his teaching he said to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in robes and to receive greetings in the marketplaces,
and to have the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.
They devour widows' houses and make long prayers for show. They will receive a harsher condemnation.”
Jesus sat down opposite the treasury and watched how the crowd put copper coins into the treasury. Many rich people were putting in large amounts.
One poor widow came and put in two lepta, which make one quadrans.
He called his disciples to him and said to them, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those putting money into the treasury.
For they all put in money out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had, her entire livelihood.
As he was leaving the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, look at these stones and these buildings!”
Jesus answered him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be torn down.”
As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,
“Tell us, when will this happen, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be fulfilled?”
Jesus began to answer them, “Be on your guard so that no one deceives you.
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and they will deceive many.
When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and unrest.

These are the beginning of the birth pains. But be on your guard. They will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them.
And the good news must first be proclaimed among all nations.

When they lead you away and hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what you will say, or rehearse it. Instead, say whatever is given to you at that moment, for it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.
You will be hated by everyone because of my name. But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
When you see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet standing where it should not be—let the reader understand—then those who are in Judea must flee to the mountains.
Anyone on the roof must not go down into the house or enter it to take anything from the house.
Anyone in the field must not turn back to get their clothes.
But woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing children in those days!
Pray that your flight will not take place in winter.
For those days will bring suffering unlike anything that has happened from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and nothing like it will ever happen again.
If the Lord had not shortened those days, no one would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen, whom he chose, he will shorten the days.
Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘Look, there he is!’ do not believe it.
For false Christs and false prophets will arise and perform signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even the chosen.
But be on your guard. See, I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that suffering, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
And the stars will begin to fall from heaven, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds with great power and glory.
And then he will send his angels and gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
Now learn the lesson of the fig tree: when its branches become tender and its leaves sprout, you know that the harvest is near.
So also, when you see these things happening, know that he is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But no one knows about that day or hour, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son, but only the Father.
Be on your guard and pray, for you do not know when the time will come.
It is like a man going away who left his house, gave his servants authority, assigned each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.
Stay awake, then, for you do not know when the master of the house will come—in the evening, at midnight, at the crowing of the rooster, or in the morning.
Otherwise, he may come suddenly and find you sleeping.
And what I say to you, I say to everyone: Stay awake.
Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away. And the chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to seize him by deceit and kill him.
But they said, “Not during the festival, lest there be an uproar among the people.”

And while he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, reclining at the table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume made from pure nard. She broke the alabaster jar and poured it over his head.
But some were indignant among themselves and said, “Why has this perfume been wasted?
For this perfume could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.
But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has done a good deed for me.
For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you wish, you can do good to them. But you do not always have me.
She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for burial.
Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to betray him to them.
When they heard this, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver coins. And he looked for a way to betray him at a suitable time.
And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover lamb, his disciples said to him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover meal?”
And he sent two of his disciples and said to them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying water in an earthenware jar will meet you. Follow him.”
“And wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’”
“And he will show you a large upstairs room, furnished and ready. Prepare for us there.”
And his two disciples went out and came into the city. They found everything just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when evening came, he arrived with the twelve.
And as they were reclining at the table and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with me will betray me.”
They began to grieve and be distressed, and to say to him one by one, “Is it I?” And another said, “Is it I?”
He answered them, “One of the twelve, who dips with me into the dish.”

“The Son of Man indeed goes as it is written about him. But woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born. But woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.”
And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “Take it; this is my body.”
And he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
And he said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, poured out for many.”
“Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
And after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
And Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away because of me this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter.’”
“But after I rise, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
But Peter said to him, “Even if everyone falls away, I will not.”
And Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today, this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
But he insisted all the more, “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” And they all said the same.
They came to a village called Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples, “Sit here while I go and pray.”
And he took Peter, James, and John with him, and began to be deeply alarmed and distressed.
And he said to them, “My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
And going a little farther, he fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.
And he said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible for you. Take this cup away from me. Yet not what I want, but what you want.”
And he came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for one hour?”
Stay awake and pray so that you do not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.
And again he went away and prayed, saying the same words.
And when he returned, he found them asleep again, for their eyes were heavy. And they did not know what to answer him.
And he came a third time and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest. The end has arrived; the hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
Get up, let us go. Look, the one who betrays me has drawn near.”
And immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd with weapons and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
Now the one who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him and lead him away securely.”
And when he arrived, he immediately approached him and said, “Rabbi, Rabbi!” And he kissed him.
And they laid hands on him and seized him.
But one of those standing nearby drew a sword, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.
And Jesus said to them, “Have you come out with weapons and clubs to arrest me as though I were a robber?
Every day I was among you, teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But let the Scriptures be fulfilled.”
And they all deserted him and fled.
And a certain young man followed him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body. And the young men seized him.
But he left the linen cloth behind and fled from them naked.
And they led Jesus to the high priest. And all the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes gathered around him.
And Peter followed him at a distance, right into the high priest’s courtyard. And he sat with the servants, warming himself by the firelight.
Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death, but they found none.
For many gave false testimony against him, but their testimonies did not agree.
And some stood up and gave false testimony against him, saying,
“We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple made by human hands, and in three days I will build another, not made by human hands.’”
But even then their testimony did not agree.
And the high priest stood up in their midst and questioned Jesus, saying, “Have you no answer? What is this testimony these men are giving against you?”
But he remained silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest questioned him and said to him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
And Jesus said, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
The high priest tore his robes and said, “Why do we still need witnesses?”
“You have heard his blasphemy. What do you think?” And they all condemned him as deserving death.
Some began to spit on him, cover his face, torment him, and say to him, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who struck you?” And the servants took him and slapped him in the face.
While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest’s servant girls came.
When she saw Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, “You too were with Jesus of Nazareth.”
But he denied it, saying, “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.” He went outside into the outer courtyard, and a rooster crowed.
When the servant girl saw him again, she began saying to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”
But he denied it again. A little later, those standing nearby again said to Peter, “You really are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech is like theirs.”
But he began to call down curses on himself and swear, “I do not know this man you are talking about.”
The rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” And he began to weep.
Immediately in the morning, the chief priests, the elders, the scribes, and the whole council held a consultation. They bound Jesus, [?], and handed him over to Pilate.
Pilate asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” He answered him, “You say so.”
The chief priests made many accusations against him, but he answered nothing.
Pilate questioned him again, saying, “Are you not going to answer anything? Look how much testimony they bring against you.”
But Jesus gave no further answer, so that Pilate was amazed.
At every feast he would release for them one prisoner whom they requested.
A man called Barabbas was imprisoned with his fellow rebels, who had committed murder during the rebellion.
They shouted and began asking him to do as he always did for them.
Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release the king of the Jews for you?”
For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas for them instead.
Pilate answered again and said to them, “What, then, do you want me to do with the one you call the king of the Jews?”
They shouted again, “Crucify him!”
Pilate said to them, “Why? What evil has he done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify him!”
Wanting to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas for them. He had Jesus flogged and handed him over to be crucified.
The soldiers led Jesus inside the courtyard, that is, the Praetorium, and called together the whole cohort.
They dressed him in purple, wove a crown of thorns, and put it on him.
They began to greet him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They struck him on the head with a reed and spat on him. Bending their knees, they bowed down before him.
When they had mocked him, they took the purple garment off him and dressed him in his own clothes. Then they led him out to crucify him.
They compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the countryside, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
They brought him to the place called Golgotha, which means “Place of a Skull.”
They offered him sour wine to drink, but he did not take it.
They crucified him and divided his clothes, casting lots for them to decide who would take what.
It was the third hour when they crucified him.
The inscription stating the charge against him read: “The King of the Jews.”
They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and the other on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled that says, “He was counted among lawbreakers.”
Those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who destroy the temple and build it in three days,
save yourself and come down from the cross!”
Likewise, the chief priests, mocking him among themselves with the scribes, said to one another, “He saved others, but he cannot save himself.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe.” Those crucified with him also reviled him.
When the sixth hour came, darkness fell over the whole land until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lima sabachthani,” which means, “God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
Some of those standing nearby heard this and said, “Look, he is calling Elijah.”
One man ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink, saying, “Leave him alone. Let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
Jesus gave a loud cry and breathed his last.
The curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
When the centurion standing opposite him saw that he cried out like this and breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God.”
There were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
who had followed him and served him when he was in Galilee, and many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
It was already evening, since it was the Preparation for Passover, that is, the day before the Sabbath.
Joseph of Arimathea came, a respected council member who was himself waiting for the kingdom of God. He boldly went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Pilate wondered whether he was already dead. Summoning the centurion, [?] whether he was already dead.
When he learned from the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
Joseph bought a linen cloth, took him down, and wrapped him in the linen cloth. He laid him in a tomb that had been cut out of rock and rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary of Joses watched where he was laid.
When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary of James, and Salome bought spices so that they could go and anoint him.
Very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
They were saying to one another, “Who will roll the stone away from the entrance to the tomb for us?”
Looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was very large.
Entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, dressed in a white robe, and they were alarmed.
He said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look at the place where he was laid.
But go and tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you.”
They went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had seized them. They said nothing to anyone, because they were afraid.
After Jesus rose early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had driven out seven demons.
She went and told those who had been with him, who were mourning and weeping.
When they heard that he was alive and that she had seen him, they did not believe.
After this, he appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking into the countryside.
Those two went and told the others, but they did not believe them either.
Later he appeared to the eleven themselves as they reclined at a meal. He rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen him risen from the dead.
He said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to all creation.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new languages;
they will pick up snakes in their hands; and if they drink anything deadly, it will not harm them at all. They will lay their hands on the sick, and they will recover.”
So the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
And they went out and preached everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word through the signs that followed. Amen. THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MARK.
